creator: Alexander Terp
description:
Measured in round 1 (2026-09-24), release build, sample profile of a scratch window during focus changes: applying a view costs about 2 ms of main-thread CPU, and about 55% of that is the sidebar. reloadData(forRowIndexes:) rebuilds each row whose keyboard marker moved, at about 1.2 ms of AppKit view construction per row: two rows per focus change, one per agent transition (which costs 2-4 ms in all). Another ~30% is AppKit retitling the window, which really does change on a focus change; ~15% is RegionView.apply.

Not per keystroke or per byte, so not the snappiness problem - but it is the largest remaining main-thread cost per user action, and it grows with agent churn. Reuse row views (update the marker and state in place) rather than reloading the row. view.received and pane_state.received carry cpu_ms, so the before/after is one grep.
title: 🐢 The sidebar rebuilds a row's views instead of reusing them
